# Decision ledger

**Scope:** Product, interface, demo, hardening, release, and upgrade decisions.
**Owner:** Engineering.
**Last verified:** 2026-11-01.

| ID | Decision | Alternatives considered | Rationale | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D4-01 | Use the **Ghostlight Hacker Workshop** theme | Generic SaaS landing, bright productivity app, pure terminal | Fits the existing haunted-workshop product while keeping a readable contemporary interface | Deep navy foundation, amber work light, spectral blue accents, layered paper/blueprint/glass/terminal surfaces |
| D4-02 | Keep the landing page at `/` and the real workshop at `/workshop` | Replace the workshop with a landing page; use a hash route | A first-time visitor needs a product explanation; the workshop needs a stable direct URL | Three routes (`/`, `/demo`, `/workshop`) with SPA fallback |
| D4-03 | Add a separate deterministic demo at `/demo` | Put fixture controls inside the real workshop; use a video only | Keeps fixture data out of the live workflow and gives visual tests stable states | The demo is explicitly labeled; it never calls a model |
| D4-04 | Lazy-load the workshop and demo | One large bundle | Landing is the first visit; workshop-specific Motion/API code should not block it | Initial JS 193.8 KiB gzip; workshop chunk 54.9 KiB; demo 11.5 KiB |
| D4-05 | Do not add an animation framework | GSAP, Lottie, Rive, Three.js | Motion and CSS already cover entry, state, and transitions; measured need is low | No new runtime; animation stays small and state-bound |
| D4-06 | Draw the four spirits as original inline SVG | Generated character images; copied mascots | Crisp at every size, tiny, themeable, accessible, state-driven, and provably original | Characters are code in `SpiritCharacter.tsx`; every state is a class |
| D4-07 | Generate one original hero image with the authorized image tool | Pure CSS landscape; stock photo; no hero image | The prompt calls for a cinematic workshop with atmospheric depth and copy space; generation was authorized | Master + responsive AVIF/WebP/JPEG outputs, prompt/provenance documented; no text/logos/watermarks |
| D4-08 | Keep source masters out of the shipped bundle | Ship the master and resize in the browser | Avoids multi-hundred-KiB downloads and layout shift | `assets/source/` is separate from `public/assets/hero/`; explicit dimensions in `<picture>` |
| D4-09 | Use semantic stage navigation, not disabled buttons | Keep disabled tab buttons | Disabled buttons are skipped by keyboard focus and imply interactivity | `<nav><ol><li aria-current="step">` with mini spirits and state text |
| D4-10 | Use native `<dialog>` for setup help | Custom modal | Built-in focus trapping, Escape behavior, and backdrop semantics | Opening help never implies the engine is connected |
| D4-11 | Use tabbed setup commands with roving tabindex | Static code blocks | The landing must show several tested commands without a wall of code | Arrow/Home/End keyboard support and copy action |
| D4-12 | Keep workflow authorization semantics stable during the interface refactor | Refactor approvals while restyling | Approval/authority semantics are security-sensitive | Phase 4 did not change exact-version approvals, Maker scope, or native denial; Phase 8 later hardened the HTTP/token layer without weakening them |
| D4-13 | Make the deterministic demo read-only | Let visitors run fake actions | Fake actions would undermine the honesty claim | Fixture controls step through states; real actions live in `/workshop` |
| D4-14 | Commit Playwright visual snapshots | Manual screenshots only | The prompt requires visual snapshots and keyboard/contrast/reduced-motion checks | `npm run test:visual`; snapshots in `tests/visual/snapshots/` |
| D4-15 | Prefer system Chrome/Chromium for visual tests, with Playwright fallback | Require a fixed browser download | Works in the verified Linux environment without a second browser install | `PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE` is honored; otherwise Playwright's browser is used |
| D4-16 | Do not use fabricated social proof | Testimonials, counts, awards | The product has no measured users or endorsements | Landing copy states the absence of fabricated claims |
| D4-17 | Remove Node `--watch` from the default dev script | Keep watch and require `.env` | Pinned Node crashes watching a missing `.env`; default setup must work from a clean checkout | `npm run dev` is stable; `npm run dev:watch` is opt-in with `.env` |
| D4-18 | Keep the hero image decorative and put all meaning in HTML | Put product copy in the image | Accessibility, localization, and performance | Hero `<picture>` is `aria-hidden`; headings and CTAs are real text |
| D4-19 | Merge the first-run connection/discovery wizard into the workshop route | Keep the merged version's workshop at `/` and rebuild onboarding as a separate app | A visitor needs the landing page first, but the real workflow still needs a guided connection step | `/workshop` shows onboarding when OpenCode is reachable without a selected model; an unavailable engine keeps the workshop visible with a repair action |
| D4-20 | Discover models, providers, agents, and permissions instead of assuming a fixed model | Keep the old fixed DeepSeek assumption | The merged OpenCode integration correctly treats the catalog as server-owned and time-limited | A model must be reported by OpenCode; a disappeared model blocks a run; provider keys stay in OpenCode |
| D4-21 | Keep the advanced OpenCode panel collapsed behind `<details>` | Put all session/permission controls in the main four-stage layout | Model/session controls are power-user surfaces; the main workflow should stay readable | Advanced controls remain reachable but do not compete with the current stage |
| D4-22 | Preserve the remote onboarding commit and integrate it rather than overwrite it | Push the Phase 4 commit over the remote or discard onboarding | The remote work is user work and adds required connection functionality | Both histories preserved through integration; 111 tests pass in the Phase 9 candidate |

## Phase 7 — guided demo

| ID | Decision | Alternatives considered | Rationale | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D7-01 | Use a versioned browser-bundled fixture | Server endpoint; live model call; video only | Deterministic playback must work without network, provider, or credentials | `src/shared/demo.ts`; no `/api/` call from `/demo` |
| D7-02 | Extract browser-safe workflow schemas to `src/shared/workflow.ts` | Duplicate schemas in the demo | One production contract; drift fails a test | Server model re-exports the shared schemas; fixture is parsed by `projectSchema` |
| D7-03 | Use the Campus Umbrella Relay scenario | Invent a new sponsor product | It aligns with the existing campus lost-and-found fixture and needs no real campus data | Clear lost-and-found scenario; no fabricated sponsor/user/metric |
| D7-04 | Reuse `RunInspector`, `SpiritStageTabs`, `SpiritCharacter`, `StatusChip` | Build a parallel demo UI | The acceptance criterion is that live and demo runs share contracts | Demo is a guided use of the production surfaces |
| D7-05 | Use a pure playback reducer | Timer/state scattered in the component | Reset/pause/replay/route-refresh behavior must be testable and isolated | `src/web/demo/playback.ts`; unit tests cover transitions |
| D7-06 | Pause playback when a spirit tab is inspected | Keep playing under the user | Inspection should not move the content under the reader | Selecting a tab pauses; Play resumes |
| D7-07 | Make presentation mode 10 beats × 9 seconds | A separate video file | Exactly 90 seconds, deterministic, recordable, and no media dependency | `?presentation=1`; optional normal mode remains |
| D7-08 | Label the fixture PASS and the live session `NOT_RUN` | Show only a passing check | The demo must not imply live execution | Run Inspector shows both rows; source label stays visible |
| D7-09 | Reject every non-GET `/api/*` request in hosted-demo mode | Rely on disabled buttons | Server authority must not depend on the UI | `DEMO_READ_ONLY`; no session token; live store unchanged |
| D7-10 | Keep reset client-only | Add a reset API | Reset must never affect a live project or OpenCode session | Pure reducer; no `/api/` request |
| D7-11 | Add three distinct landing actions | One ambiguous “demo” CTA | Visitors and judges need to choose interactive, presentation, or live | Try the example, Watch the guided workflow, Run live with OpenCode |
| D7-12 | Keep the fixture source free of time/randomness/environment/network | Generate fixture at runtime | Deterministic playback and reproducible screenshots | Source scan test; fixed timestamps and content hashes |

## Phase 8 — security and recovery hardening

| ID | Decision | Alternatives considered | Rationale | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D8-01 | Use one canonical `UB_DEPLOYMENT_MODE` (`local`, `hosted-demo`, `private-hosted`) | Keep parallel `UB_MODE` values | Two mode dialects caused contradictory docs and startup behavior | Legacy alias accepted; `hosted-private` and `private-hosted` map to the same mode |
| D8-02 | Make hosted-demo public and read-only, not password-protected | Reuse the private Basic Auth path for the demo | The demo contains no user data, secret, engine, or mutation; requiring credentials would make the judge path worse | No token, no OpenCode, every non-GET `/api/*` → `DEMO_READ_ONLY` |
| D8-03 | Require session token on protected API reads as well as writes | Token only on mutations | State, connection, discovery, usage, and exports can contain project/native metadata | Browser client obtains the token once; manual API checks need the header |
| D8-04 | Reject paid or unpriced remote models at selection | Accept any discovered model and rely on cost afterward | The release promises no paid fallback | Superseded for new projects by U1-01; migrated projects retain this as the default policy |
| D8-05 | Keep async Maker runs with explicit UNKNOWN/WAITING_PERMISSION states | Revert to a synchronous blocking request | Long native work must not hold the HTTP request; restart/reconnect must be honest | `202` accepted; polling/SSE, cancel/reconcile; no automatic retry |
| D8-06 | Refuse to mark cancellation when native interruption fails | Mark CANCELLED anyway | Native effects may continue | Explicit `CANCEL_UNAVAILABLE`; reconcile instead |
| D8-07 | Use a lock, fsync, backups, quarantine, and state v2 | Single overwrite or reset-on-corrupt | Approvals and evidence must survive crashes | Recovery is visible; both-corrupt state refuses reset |
| D8-08 | Apply SSRF/workspace/origin/rate/size controls in one server pipeline | Rely on the browser or deployment proxy alone | Server authority must not depend on UI or platform assumptions | Deterministic security tests cover the pipeline |
| D8-09 | Keep Backboard unintegrated and unclaimed | Add a placeholder key/adapter for category optics | Installation alone is not meaningful use and no access exists | No Backboard category claim |

## Phase 9 — release gate

| ID | Decision | Alternatives considered | Rationale | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D9-01 | Integrate the guided-interface and hardening lines before verifying | Pick one line and document the other as future work | Each line contains a required MUST; dropping either breaks acceptance | One release candidate with both feature sets |
| D9-02 | Treat the public demo's no-auth behavior as canonical over the earlier hardening test | Keep the older "demo requires token/password" test | The final mode contract and product promise make the demo public/read-only | Test updated to assert private-hosted protection instead |
| D9-03 | Update async-run tests instead of reverting the async runner | Force synchronous behavior to satisfy older tests | Async queue/restart/reconnect is the implemented, safer UX | Tests poll persisted state; no retry/duplicate inference |
| D9-04 | Move superseded planning/setup docs to `docs/history/` with pointers | Leave conflicting root docs active | One canonical story is required | Canonical docs + archived provenance |
| D9-05 | Keep the four runtime prompts in `docs/prompts/` unchanged | Rename/archive them with the implementation docs | Loaders and runtime discovery must not be confused with phase history | Prompt filenames/loaders stay stable |
| D9-06 | Report the unresolved moderate audit advisory honestly | Force a breaking Sentry downgrade without verification | A forced major downgrade could break telemetry and source maps | Production audit at high level passes; advisory documented |
| D9-07 | Stop before deployment/publication/submission | Treat local verification as release authorization | External actions need separate scoped authority | Evidence and reviewable procedures only |

## Upgrade Phase 0 — product-upgrade preparation

| ID | Decision | Alternatives considered | Rationale | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| U0-01 | Introduce schema v3 as an additive persisted contract | Mutate v2 in place; defer schema work until features ship | Later phases need stable fields without risking existing approvals/evidence | Explicit v1/v2 readers and one canonical v3 writer |
| U0-02 | Make migration deterministic and idempotent with a fixed missing-time sentinel | Fill missing legacy timestamps with migration time | Wall-clock defaults make repeat migration produce different state | `1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z` marks an unavailable legacy timestamp honestly |
---UPGRADE---
| U4-03 | Require an explicit accept/reject decision and bind it to the candidate base version/hash | Accept by latest content; auto-accept if the contract passes | A section can change while a candidate is being reviewed; silent overwrite is unacceptable | Accept fails with a conflict if the base changed; the user can request a fresh candidate or discard the old one |
| U4-04 | Keep acceptance separate from approval | Treat accepting a revision as approval | The user may accept wording but still want a separate approval gate; approvals are exact-version security boundaries | Accepting sets the section to `DRAFT` at the candidate version; `approveSection` remains the only path to `APPROVED` |
| U4-05 | Mark the accepted section's approval and every transitive dependent approval stale | Mark all sections stale; leave downstream approvals untouched | Only sections whose inputs changed need review; unrelated approvals should stay valid | The accepted section becomes `DRAFT`; dependent `APPROVED` sections become `STALE` and their approvals record the upstream change |
| U4-06 | Render a safe Markdown subset with React text nodes and filtered links | `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`; a permissive Markdown/HTML pipeline | Generated content is untrusted model output; raw HTML and `javascript:` links must never execute | Headings, paragraphs, lists, emphasis, links, tables, and code render without HTML injection; unsafe links are reduced to their labels |
| U4-07 | Use a shared line diff for unified and side-by-side views, defaulting by screen width | Separate diff implementations; always side-by-side | Both views must describe the same change, and narrow screens cannot show two readable columns | One LCS diff feeds both views; side-by-side is the wide default and stacks with labels on narrow screens |
| U4-08 | Migrate v1–v6 projects explicitly to schema v7 | Reset candidates; keep v6 and silently default new fields | Existing projects and audit history must remain usable | Legacy candidates gain deterministic base/summary/decision defaults; no IDs or timestamps are invented |

## Upgrade Phase 5 — focused workshop and reorganized OpenCode controls

| ID | Decision | Alternatives considered | Rationale | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| U5-01 | Present one primary task and move outline, memory, and activity into disclosure drawers | Keep the three-column permanent rail; add more panels beside the main task | The main task must be understandable without opening technical machinery, and empty panels should not reserve space | The main document is a single centered column; outline and memory are collapsed `<details>` drawers |
| U5-02 | Rename Run Inspector to **Activity & results** and organize it into Progress, Changes, and Checks | Keep one mixed “native runs” list | Users need to know whether a run is progressing, what changed, and what was actually checked without reading technical rows | The first three sections answer those questions; the component keeps the read-only honesty note |
| U5-03 | Hide Activity & results when no operation or evidence exists | Show an empty inspector permanently | An empty technical panel is visual noise and implies a run exists | The drawer is omitted until relevant; an active or abandoned run opens it automatically |
| U5-04 | Move native IDs, capability mappings, raw evidence, provider payloads, and the transcript under Technical details or Advanced diagnostics | Show IDs and raw rows in the primary view | Operational facts are useful but not the main task; raw transcripts are diagnostic material | Primary sections stay readable; the technical disclosure remains available and redacted |
| U5-05 | Replace Session notes with Project memory covering decisions, user answers, assumptions, constraints, and unresolved questions | Keep the latest transcript excerpts as the memory surface | Users need the durable project record, not a truncated chat feed | Project memory is editable; the raw transcript moves to Advanced diagnostics |
| U5-06 | Persist memory edits through `POST /api/memory`, appending a new active entry and superseding the corrected one | Mutate an existing entry in place; add a second state schema | The existing memory shape already supports status/supersedesId; audit history must survive corrections | Corrections are explicit and auditable; no schema migration is required |
| U5-07 | Split OpenCode controls into Model & connection, a contextual permission request, and Advanced diagnostics; load advanced data only on open | Keep one `<details>` containing every harness control; load sessions/usage on mount | Permissions must be impossible to miss, while sessions, agents, commands, skills, MCP, LSP, formatters, revert, export, and transcripts are diagnostic | The permission alert sits outside collapsed details; advanced sessions/usage are fetched when the panel opens |
| U5-08 | Keep the focused layout accessible on mobile and keyboard; move focus to the main task on stage change and announce busy/permission state | Rely on visual placement and native details behavior alone | The layout change must not make the workflow unreachable by keyboard or screen reader | Drawers are native disclosures, the main task receives focus after a stage change, and a polite live region reports run/permission state |
| U5-09 | Raise the all-JS gzip budget from 280 to 290 KiB | Shrink the new memory/diagnostics surfaces until the old budget passes | The focused workshop adds a real project-memory surface and lazy diagnostics without removing functionality | The measured build is 280.7 KiB all JS; the increase is recorded in the UX budget rather than silently accepted |

## Open follow-ups (post-release)

- A real recorded demo and final submission assets remain separate acceptance work.
- The free-model route remains account-dependent and time-limited.
- A public hosted URL is not asserted until a deployment is verified.
- Any future change to the asset budget or claims requires updating `docs/UX_AND_VISUAL_SYSTEM.md` and `docs/PRODUCT_BRIEF.md`.

# Architecture — Unfinished Business

**Status:** Upgrade Phase 5 (focused workshop and reorganized OpenCode controls) implemented on the verified Phase 4 baseline.
**Owner:** Engineering.
**Last verified:** 2026-11-01 against the Phase 5 verification matrix recorded in `docs/EVIDENCE.md`.

## 1. System shape

```text
Browser
  ├─ /            landing page (eager)
  ├─ /demo        deterministic walkthrough (lazy chunk)
  └─ /workshop    real workshop (lazy chunk)
        │
        │ same-origin fetch /api/*
        │ Basic Auth in hosted modes; x-ub-session-token on protected API routes
        ▼
Hono server (src/server/app.ts)
  ├─ /api/health                 public, minimal
  ├─ /api/mode                   public mode descriptor
  ├─ /api/session                token issue (loopback/local, Basic Auth/private)
  ├─ /api/runtime                effective limits/retention
  ├─ /api/engine                 connection/engine summary
  ├─ /api/connection*            check, configure (local only), reset
  ├─ /api/opencode/*             discovery, project-owned sessions, permissions, usage
  ├─ /api/engine/selection       persist a discovered model allowed by project policy
  ├─ /api/model-preferences      access mode, privacy preference, optional spending limit
  ├─ /api/project, /api/export   snapshot/approved plan; workspace paths omitted
  ├─ /api/project/source*        select source; explicitly confirm managed remote import
  ├─ /api/events                 authenticated bounded SSE snapshots
---
- the run coordinator records progress phases through safe polling (`session.get`, `message.list`, `permission.request.list`) plus directed callbacks from the native guide; prompts, raw model text, and unvalidated JSON are never persisted as progress;
- a timeout, disconnect, or restart leaves the operation `ABANDONED` with an `AWAITING_RECONCILIATION` marker and its native session reference; it blocks new runs until reconciled but never permanently blocks the project;
- reconciliation observes the native outcome, retrieves the actual late reply or diff through fresh reads, validates it with the same schemas as live completions, and applies it at most once (`appliedAt` plus the idempotent action record); an idle session alone is never success;
- `POST /api/runs/:id/retry` starts a new Maker operation with `retryOf` lineage after a confirmed `FAILED` outcome; uncertain runs must be reconciled first;
- `POST /api/runs/:id/abandon` records a user decision on an outstanding operation when no in-process runner is active;
- startup marks in-flight work `ABANDONED` with a recovery marker; reconciliation reads native state and never replays automatically;
- evidence records an observed native result/fingerprint; a missing result is an empty state.

`AtomicProjectStore` acquires a cross-process lock, writes a private temp file, fsyncs, renames, keeps `.previous` and rolling `backups/`, quarantines corrupt current files, and prunes bounded retention. A corrupt current with no valid previous returns `STATE_CORRUPT`; it never silently resets.

## 8. Demo fixture boundaries

The deterministic demo is a browser-bundled fixture, not a server response and not a parallel UI:

```text
src/shared/workflow.ts   production Zod schemas + types
        │
        ├─ src/server/workflow/model.ts  hashing, migration, persistence helpers
        ├─ src/shared/demo.ts            versioned fixture + playback beats
        └─ src/web/demo/DemoPage.tsx     playback + shared components
                    │
                    ├─ RunInspector
                    ├─ SpiritStageTabs (inspect variant)
                    ├─ SpiritCharacter / StatusChip / Brand
                    └─ pure playback reducer (no API calls)
```

`src/shared/demo.ts` has no `node:`, `fetch`, `process.env`, `Date.now`, or `Math.random`. Tests parse the fixture with the production schemas and recompute section hashes. Every fixture result is labeled; the live session remains `NOT_RUN`.

In `hosted-demo` mode the server independently returns the fixture from `/api/project` and `/api/export`, returns a read-only connection status, rejects `/api/session` and every non-GET `/api/*` request, and never constructs an OpenCode connection.

## 9. Trust boundaries and residual risks

| Boundary | Enforced controls |
|---|---|
| Browser → app | Host/Origin/CSRF policy, Basic Auth in hosted modes, constant-time session token, JSON content type, request-size cap, rate/concurrency limits |
| App → disk | Canonical roots, traversal/symlink rejection, regular-file checks, `0700` directories, `0600` files, lock, fsync, previous snapshot, backups, quarantine |
| App → OpenCode | URL syntax, loopback default, HTTPS and explicit host allowlist for remote, optional port allowlist, DNS/IP classification, redirect refusal, timeout, response cap, version/auth/model readiness |
| App → repository source | Canonical local-directory policy; public HTTPS-only remote URL; embedded-credential rejection; managed workspace; explicit confirmation before import; no Maker write authority in Phase 3; paths omitted from browser/model |
| OpenCode → provider | Native credentials, permissions, sessions; the app never reads provider keys |
| App → Sentry | Collection disabled, event/breadcrumb scrubbing, metadata-only spans, no prompts/tool args/results/local paths |

| D7-02 | Extract browser-safe workflow schemas to `src/shared/workflow.ts` | Duplicate schemas in the demo | One production contract; drift fails a test | Server model re-exports the shared schemas; fixture is parsed by `projectSchema` |
| D7-03 | Use the Campus Umbrella Relay scenario | Invent a new sponsor product | It aligns with the existing campus lost-and-found fixture and needs no real campus data | Clear lost-and-found scenario; no fabricated sponsor/user/metric |
| D7-04 | Reuse `RunInspector`, `SpiritStageTabs`, `SpiritCharacter`, `StatusChip` | Build a parallel demo UI | The acceptance criterion is that live and demo runs share contracts | Demo is a guided use of the production surfaces |
| D7-05 | Use a pure playback reducer | Timer/state scattered in the component | Reset/pause/replay/route-refresh behavior must be testable and isolated | `src/web/demo/playback.ts`; unit tests cover transitions |
| D7-06 | Pause playback when a spirit tab is inspected | Keep playing under the user | Inspection should not move the content under the reader | Selecting a tab pauses; Play resumes |
| D7-07 | Make presentation mode 10 beats × 9 seconds | A separate video file | Exactly 90 seconds, deterministic, recordable, and no media dependency | `?presentation=1`; optional normal mode remains |
| D7-08 | Label the fixture PASS and the live session `NOT_RUN` | Show only a passing check | The demo must not imply live execution | Run Inspector shows both rows; source label stays visible |
| D7-09 | Reject every non-GET `/api/*` request in hosted-demo mode | Rely on disabled buttons | Server authority must not depend on the UI | `DEMO_READ_ONLY`; no session token; live store unchanged |
| D7-10 | Keep reset client-only | Add a reset API | Reset must never affect a live project or OpenCode session | Pure reducer; no `/api/` request |
| D7-11 | Add three distinct landing actions | One ambiguous “demo” CTA | Visitors and judges need to choose interactive, presentation, or live | Try the example, Watch the guided workflow, Run live with OpenCode |
| D7-12 | Keep the fixture source free of time/randomness/environment/network | Generate fixture at runtime | Deterministic playback and reproducible screenshots | Source scan test; fixed timestamps and content hashes |

## Phase 8 — security and recovery hardening

| ID | Decision | Alternatives considered | Rationale | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D8-01 | Use one canonical `UB_DEPLOYMENT_MODE` (`local`, `hosted-demo`, `private-hosted`) | Keep parallel `UB_MODE` values | Two mode dialects caused contradictory docs and startup behavior | Legacy alias accepted; `hosted-private` and `private-hosted` map to the same mode |
| D8-02 | Make hosted-demo public and read-only, not password-protected | Reuse the private Basic Auth path for the demo | The demo contains no user data, secret, engine, or mutation; requiring credentials would make the judge path worse | No token, no OpenCode, every non-GET `/api/*` → `DEMO_READ_ONLY` |
| D8-03 | Require session token on protected API reads as well as writes | Token only on mutations | State, connection, discovery, usage, and exports can contain project/native metadata | Browser client obtains the token once; manual API checks need the header |
| D8-04 | Reject paid or unpriced remote models at selection | Accept any discovered model and rely on cost afterward | The release promises no paid fallback | Superseded for new projects by U1-01; migrated projects retain this as the default policy |
| D8-05 | Keep async Maker runs with explicit UNKNOWN/WAITING_PERMISSION states | Revert to a synchronous blocking request | Long native work must not hold the HTTP request; restart/reconnect must be honest | `202` accepted; polling/SSE, cancel/reconcile; no automatic retry |
| D8-06 | Refuse to mark cancellation when native interruption fails | Mark CANCELLED anyway | Native effects may continue | Explicit `CANCEL_UNAVAILABLE`; reconcile instead |
| D8-07 | Use a lock, fsync, backups, quarantine, and state v2 | Single overwrite or reset-on-corrupt | Approvals and evidence must survive crashes | Recovery is visible; both-corrupt state refuses reset |
| D8-08 | Apply SSRF/workspace/origin/rate/size controls in one server pipeline | Rely on the browser or deployment proxy alone | Server authority must not depend on UI or platform assumptions | Deterministic security tests cover the pipeline |
| D8-09 | Keep Backboard unintegrated and unclaimed | Add a placeholder key/adapter for category optics | Installation alone is not meaningful use and no access exists | No Backboard category claim |

## Phase 9 — release gate

| ID | Decision | Alternatives considered | Rationale | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D9-01 | Integrate the guided-interface and hardening lines before verifying | Pick one line and document the other as future work | Each line contains a required MUST; dropping either breaks acceptance | One release candidate with both feature sets |
| D9-02 | Treat the public demo's no-auth behavior as canonical over the earlier hardening test | Keep the older "demo requires token/password" test | The final mode contract and product promise make the demo public/read-only | Test updated to assert private-hosted protection instead |
| D9-03 | Update async-run tests instead of reverting the async runner | Force synchronous behavior to satisfy older tests | Async queue/restart/reconnect is the implemented, safer UX | Tests poll persisted state; no retry/duplicate inference |
| D9-04 | Move superseded planning/setup docs to `docs/history/` with pointers | Leave conflicting root docs active | One canonical story is required | Canonical docs + archived provenance |
| D9-05 | Keep the four runtime prompts in `docs/prompts/` unchanged | Rename/archive them with the implementation docs | Loaders and runtime discovery must not be confused with phase history | Prompt filenames/loaders stay stable |
| D9-06 | Report the unresolved moderate audit advisory honestly | Force a breaking Sentry downgrade without verification | A forced major downgrade could break telemetry and source maps | Production audit at high level passes; advisory documented |
| D9-07 | Stop before deployment/publication/submission | Treat local verification as release authorization | External actions need separate scoped authority | Evidence and reviewable procedures only |

## Upgrade Phase 0 — product-upgrade preparation

| ID | Decision | Alternatives considered | Rationale | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| U0-01 | Introduce schema v3 as an additive persisted contract | Mutate v2 in place; defer schema work until features ship | Later phases need stable fields without risking existing approvals/evidence | Explicit v1/v2 readers and one canonical v3 writer |
| U0-02 | Make migration deterministic and idempotent with a fixed missing-time sentinel | Fill missing legacy timestamps with migration time | Wall-clock defaults make repeat migration produce different state | `1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z` marks an unavailable legacy timestamp honestly |
---UPGRADE---
| U4-03 | Require an explicit accept/reject decision and bind it to the candidate base version/hash | Accept by latest content; auto-accept if the contract passes | A section can change while a candidate is being reviewed; silent overwrite is unacceptable | Accept fails with a conflict if the base changed; the user can request a fresh candidate or discard the old one |
| U4-04 | Keep acceptance separate from approval | Treat accepting a revision as approval | The user may accept wording but still want a separate approval gate; approvals are exact-version security boundaries | Accepting sets the section to `DRAFT` at the candidate version; `approveSection` remains the only path to `APPROVED` |
| U4-05 | Mark the accepted section's approval and every transitive dependent approval stale | Mark all sections stale; leave downstream approvals untouched | Only sections whose inputs changed need review; unrelated approvals should stay valid | The accepted section becomes `DRAFT`; dependent `APPROVED` sections become `STALE` and their approvals record the upstream change |
| U4-06 | Render a safe Markdown subset with React text nodes and filtered links | `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`; a permissive Markdown/HTML pipeline | Generated content is untrusted model output; raw HTML and `javascript:` links must never execute | Headings, paragraphs, lists, emphasis, links, tables, and code render without HTML injection; unsafe links are reduced to their labels |
| U4-07 | Use a shared line diff for unified and side-by-side views, defaulting by screen width | Separate diff implementations; always side-by-side | Both views must describe the same change, and narrow screens cannot show two readable columns | One LCS diff feeds both views; side-by-side is the wide default and stacks with labels on narrow screens |
| U4-08 | Migrate v1–v6 projects explicitly to schema v7 | Reset candidates; keep v6 and silently default new fields | Existing projects and audit history must remain usable | Legacy candidates gain deterministic base/summary/decision defaults; no IDs or timestamps are invented |

## Upgrade Phase 5 — focused workshop and reorganized OpenCode controls

| ID | Decision | Alternatives considered | Rationale | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| U5-01 | Present one primary task and move outline, memory, and activity into disclosure drawers | Keep the three-column permanent rail; add more panels beside the main task | The main task must be understandable without opening technical machinery, and empty panels should not reserve space | The main document is a single centered column; outline and memory are collapsed `<details>` drawers |
| U5-02 | Rename Run Inspector to **Activity & results** and organize it into Progress, Changes, and Checks | Keep one mixed “native runs” list | Users need to know whether a run is progressing, what changed, and what was actually checked without reading technical rows | The first three sections answer those questions; the component keeps the read-only honesty note |
| U5-03 | Hide Activity & results when no operation or evidence exists | Show an empty inspector permanently | An empty technical panel is visual noise and implies a run exists | The drawer is omitted until relevant; an active or abandoned run opens it automatically |
| U5-04 | Move native IDs, capability mappings, raw evidence, provider payloads, and the transcript under Technical details or Advanced diagnostics | Show IDs and raw rows in the primary view | Operational facts are useful but not the main task; raw transcripts are diagnostic material | Primary sections stay readable; the technical disclosure remains available and redacted |
| U5-05 | Replace Session notes with Project memory covering decisions, user answers, assumptions, constraints, and unresolved questions | Keep the latest transcript excerpts as the memory surface | Users need the durable project record, not a truncated chat feed | Project memory is editable; the raw transcript moves to Advanced diagnostics |
| U5-06 | Persist memory edits through `POST /api/memory`, appending a new active entry and superseding the corrected one | Mutate an existing entry in place; add a second state schema | The existing memory shape already supports status/supersedesId; audit history must survive corrections | Corrections are explicit and auditable; no schema migration is required |
| U5-07 | Split OpenCode controls into Model & connection, a contextual permission request, and Advanced diagnostics; load advanced data only on open | Keep one `<details>` containing every harness control; load sessions/usage on mount | Permissions must be impossible to miss, while sessions, agents, commands, skills, MCP, LSP, formatters, revert, export, and transcripts are diagnostic | The permission alert sits outside collapsed details; advanced sessions/usage are fetched when the panel opens |
| U5-08 | Keep the focused layout accessible on mobile and keyboard; move focus to the main task on stage change and announce busy/permission state | Rely on visual placement and native details behavior alone | The layout change must not make the workflow unreachable by keyboard or screen reader | Drawers are native disclosures, the main task receives focus after a stage change, and a polite live region reports run/permission state |
| U5-09 | Raise the all-JS gzip budget from 280 to 290 KiB | Shrink the new memory/diagnostics surfaces until the old budget passes | The focused workshop adds a real project-memory surface and lazy diagnostics without removing functionality | The measured build is 280.7 KiB all JS; the increase is recorded in the UX budget rather than silently accepted |

## Open follow-ups (post-release)

- A real recorded demo and final submission assets remain separate acceptance work.
- The free-model route remains account-dependent and time-limited.
- A public hosted URL is not asserted until a deployment is verified.
- Any future change to the asset budget or claims requires updating `docs/UX_AND_VISUAL_SYSTEM.md` and `docs/PRODUCT_BRIEF.md`.

The project outline is a collapsible drawer; the permanent three-column rail and Session notes panel are gone. - The header is a compact model/connection summary. Permission requests appear as a contextual alert outside collapsed controls, so they cannot be missed. - **Run Inspector is now Activity & results**, organized into **Progress**, **Changes**, and **Checks**. It is omitted when no operation or check exists and opens automatically for an active or abandoned run. - Native session/message IDs, capability mappings, raw evidence, and provider payloads moved under **Technical details**. Raw transcripts moved to **Advanced diagnostics**. - **Project memory** replaces Session notes: decisions, user answers, assumptions, constraints, and unresolved questions are visible and editable. A correction appends a new entry and keeps the prior one as `SUPERSEDED`; it never changes an approval, draft, Maker scope, or native run. `POST /api/memory` provides the authenticated edit path. - OpenCode controls are split into **Model & connection**, a **contextual permission request**, and **Advanced diagnostics**. Sessions, agents, commands, skills, MCP, LSP, formatters, low-level revert, export, and transcripts stay in Advanced diagnostics and load only when opened. - The stage action is unambiguous: approval is primary only for a current draft; otherwise drafting or the stage's own action is primary. - Drawers are native disclosures with keyboard and focus behavior; stage changes move focus to the main task; busy and permission state are announced through a polite live region; mobile and tablet layouts avoid horizontal overflow. - Schema v7 is unchanged. The memory edit route uses the existing status/supersedesId fields, so no migration is required. - Verification passes: typecheck, **184 tests**, production build, all five bundle/asset budgets (all-JS budget deliberately raised from 280 to 290 KiB), and **19 visual/accessibility tests**. Known limits: permission polling is best-effort and can lag one refresh interval; Advanced diagnostics are unavailable while the engine is unreachable; automated accessibility checks do not replace a screen-reader audit. ### Upgrade Phase 4 — reviewable generated revisions - Architect output is now a **proposed revision**, never an immediate overwrite. “Request changes” queues an Architect run; the current draft stays visible until the user accepts the candidate. - Every Architect section has a **content contract**: required topics, detail guidance, dependencies, risk and decision requirements, acceptance criteria, and required headings. Validation is structural and topic-based, so padded word count alone cannot pass. - The review surface shows the candidate summary, the requested change, the **complete revised Markdown**, and a **unified or side-by-side diff**. Wide screens default to side-by-side; narrow screens stack the two sides with labels. - **Accept**, **Request another revision**, and **Discard** are explicit. A new request supersedes an earlier pending candidate; a candidate whose base version changed cannot be accepted. - **Accepting is not approval.** Acceptance replaces the draft and marks the section `DRAFT`; the exact-version approval remains a separate action. Accepting an upstream revision marks only transitive dependent approvals stale. - Generated Markdown is rendered safely: headings, paragraphs, lists, emphasis, links, tables, and code work; raw HTML/script is never executed and unsafe link protocols are reduced to their labels. - Schema **v7** records candidate base version/hash, summary, requested change, decision time, and status. Known limits: the Markdown subset is intentionally small (not full CommonMark); contract validation checks structure and topic coverage, not prose quality; visual snapshots do not yet capture a live candidate state. ### Upgrade Phase 3 — project intake and guided discovery - Every fresh workshop now starts with an explicit source choice: **new project**, **existing local repository**, **remote repository URL**, or **continue saved project**. Oracle cannot run until the source is confirmed. - Local repository paths pass the existing canonical workspace-security rules. Their absolute paths remain private server state and are omitted from public project responses and Oracle prompts. - Remote repositories are limited to credential-free public HTTPS URLs. Selection does not clone or grant write access; an explicit second confirmation imports into an app-managed workspace with Git prompts, credential helpers, redirects, and command output disabled. - Oracle is now a focused multi-turn interview. A turn contains at most three questions, each with a short reason and optional choices. The full Product Discovery procedure remains active instead of being replaced by a tiny one-shot JSON instruction. - Schema v6 records the complete intake with per-answer provenance, known constraints, risks, facts, user decisions, assumptions, and recommended action. Corrections supersede older memory entries without erasing history. - Proposals use a structured facts/decisions/assumptions shape. The server rejects premature proposals unless source and essential intake are present; assumed essential answers require the user to explicitly proceed with the stated assumptions. - Explicit v1–v5 migrations preserve older projects, operations, approvals, transcripts, and recovery metadata while treating legacy projects as confirmed saved work. - Phase 3 tests cover all four source paths, URL/path safety, pending remote confirmation, private-path omission, incomplete intake, question limits, prompt retention, reload persistence, proposal provenance, explicit assumptions, and corrections. - Verification passes: typecheck, 161 unit/integration tests, production build, all five bundle/asset budgets, 18 visual/accessibility tests, and the production high-severity dependency audit. Known limits: remote import supports public unauthenticated HTTPS repositories only; it does not support SSH, private repositories, credentialed URLs, submodule credentials, arbitrary redirects, or remote browser-to-local pairing. Selecting a repository does not grant Maker access to it; Maker remains bounded to its existing isolated workflow until a later phase deliberately changes that authority. ### Upgrade Phase 2 — observable, cancellable, recoverable runs - Oracle, Architect, Maker, and Witness runs are now **persisted asynchronous operations**. The request returns `202 Accepted` immediately; the saved project updates as the run progresses. The synchronous `question` adapter is the only exception because it changes no saved state. - Every queued run records **live progress phases**: connecting, session created, waiting for the model, receiving output, validating result, waiting for permission, applying result, and running checks. Phases are safe summaries — prompts and raw model output are never shown or saved as progress. - The **Activity & results** view (formerly Run Inspector) now shows elapsed time and per-run progress, and offers **Continue waiting, Reconcile now, Open in OpenCode, Cancel, Retry after failure, and Mark abandoned**. - **Reconciliation is real**: it observes the native session, retrieves the actual late reply or file diff, validates it with the same rules as normal completion, and applies it **exactly once**. An idle session is never treated as success. An unretrievable result stays `COMPLETED_UNAPPLIED` and remains reconcileable. - A timed-out or disconnected run leaves an `ABANDONED` operation with a recovery marker instead of a dead end; the project can always be reconciled, cancelled, retried, or marked abandoned. - **Retry after a confirmed failure** starts a new Maker operation with explicit `retryOf` lineage; uncertain runs must be reconciled first, so retrying can never silently duplicate a native edit. - Schema **v5** adds recovery metadata (intended action, target section, starting revision, idempotency key, expected output, retry lineage, progress phase). # Demo and submission guidance

**Status:** Guided sample and first-release evidence complete. A real recorded video, published article, deployment, and submission remain pending explicit authorization.
**Owner:** Demo/submission.
**Last verified:** 2026-11-01 (20 visual/accessibility tests; 185 unit/integration/component tests).

## Two different demos

| Demo | What it is | What it proves |
|---|---|---|
| Guided sample (`/demo`) | One versioned Driftwatch fixture played through the real interface components | Interface states, approval language, permission boundaries, evidence wording, recovery, and reset isolation |
| Real workshop (`/workshop`) | The four-stage workflow connected to a local OpenCode server | Actual native sessions, observed tool results, real failures and success |

Never present the guided sample as live inference. Never use a sample screenshot to claim a real build passed. The sample page and its fixture are deliberately separate from live project data.

## Scenario: Driftwatch

The sample revives a small abandoned open-source issue-triage CLI:

1. Driftwatch reads a local `issues.json` export and prints issues that have gone quiet.
2. The copied project parses the export, but it still counts closed issues and measures age from the creation date instead of the latest activity.
3. The Oracle clarifies one local export, a 90-day window, closed issues skipped, and age measured from the latest activity date.
4. The Architect approves eight sections; a revision narrows the first release and makes the old approval stale.
5. Maker receives a separate scope for two files in `demo-workspace/`.
6. One bounded change skips closed issues, measures the latest activity, keeps the report shape stable, and adds a behavioural test.
7. A recorded `node --test` check reports 4 passed, 0 failed.
8. Witness separates the recorded pass from the missing live proof and states the next honest step.

No real repository, maintainer, sponsor, user, metric, deployment, account, or competition result is depicted. The sample is an original story about a hackathon team reviving abandoned open-source work, not a claim about a real project.

## Fixture and provenance

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Fixture module | `src/shared/demo.ts` |
| Fixture version | `driftwatch@1` |
| Data mode | `demo` |
| Source label | `Recorded sample — not a live OpenCode session` |
| Production contract | `src/shared/workflow.ts` (`projectSchema`, operation/evidence/capability schemas) |
| Drift test | `tests/demo.test.ts` |
| Landing consistency | `tests/web.test.ts`; `tests/visual/landing.spec.ts` |
| Playback state | `src/web/demo/playback.ts` |
| UI | `src/web/demo/DemoPage.tsx`, `src/web/landing/DemoTeaser.tsx` |
| Shared components | `RunInspector`, `SpiritCharacter`, `SpiritStageTabs`, `StatusChip`, `Brand` |

The fixture contains the input idea, Oracle clarification, approved product summary, eight Architect sections, two revisions, Maker authorization, normalized operations, a representative diff, verification output, Witness findings, submission readiness, and next actions. Section hashes are real SHA-256 hashes of the fixed content and are recomputed by the test.

The fixture is browser-safe: it imports no server, filesystem, network, provider, or OpenCode module. `tests/demo.test.ts` also reads the source to assert that it has no `fetch`, `/api/`, `node:`, `Date.now`, `Math.random`, or `process.env` use.

**One canonical source.** `src/web/content/landing.ts` holds copy and configuration only. The landing preview (`demoPreviewSteps`), the evidence view, and the guided sample all read the same fixture. There is no second landing operation/evidence list and no contradictory PASS/FAIL state.

## Playback

| Control | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Play / Pause | Starts or stops deterministic auto-advance |
| Previous / Next step | Moves one beat and pauses |
| Replay | Returns to beat 1 and plays |
| Reset | Returns to beat 1, paused, and clears tab inspection |
| Spirit tabs | Inspect Oracle, Architect, Maker, or Witness at any time; inspection pauses playback |
| 90s mode | Enters the screen-recording presentation path |

Normal playback holds each of the 10 beats for 7 seconds. Presentation mode holds each beat for 9 seconds, for exactly 90 seconds. Presentation mode is optional; normal interactive use remains available. `?presentation=1` is the route-refresh state for presentation mode.

The sample uses `setTimeout` only for playback. It makes no network request, inference call, provider call, or mutation request. The Playwright test records requests during playback and asserts that no `/api/` or provider URL is contacted.

## Reset behavior

Reset is a pure reducer transition in `src/web/demo/playback.ts`. It changes only:

- the sample beat index;
- the playing/paused flag;
- the inspected spirit tab;
- the completed flag.

It cannot call `/api/*`, cannot change a live project snapshot, cannot start or stop an OpenCode session, and cannot clear live state. In hosted-sample mode the server independently rejects every non-GET `/api/*` request with `DEMO_READ_ONLY`, so a browser cannot reach a live mutation even if the UI were bypassed.

## Live-versus-recorded disclosure

| Claim | Sample behavior |
|---|---|
| “This is live inference” | **Prohibited.** The page says no provider call or model quota is used. |
| “The check passed” | Allowed only with the label “recorded sample”; the live session is shown as `NOT_RUN`. |
| “This is the visitor's repository” | **Prohibited.** The workspace is `demo://driftwatch`. |
| “This is a submitted hackathon entry” | **Prohibited.** The Witness readiness statement says it is not a submission. |
| “Reset is safe for live state” | Allowed with the exact scope: reset changes only the sample. |

Every simulated operation, evidence row, diff, and finding carries a visible `Sample data` chip or a recorded-sample source label. Activity & results receives the same operation/evidence/capability shapes as the live workshop. Provenance, fixture version, technical caveats, and the evidence inspector sit under `<details>` so the main story stays plain-language.

## Evidence boundary

- The fixture, reset isolation, schema drift, 90-second timing, tab inspection, no-network behavior, and canonical landing/demo consistency are covered by `tests/demo.test.ts`, `tests/web.test.ts`, and `tests/visual/`.
- The hosted sample was smoke-tested locally: fixture project, no session token, `DEMO_READ_ONLY` mutation, no engine, and a rendered `/demo`.

**Status:** Approved product; Upgrade Phase 5 (focused workshop and reorganized OpenCode controls) verified locally.
**Owner:** Product/interface.
**Last verified:** 2026-11-01.

## One sentence

Unfinished Business is an OpenCode-powered hackathon project builder where four friendly spirits guide one unfinished idea through a clear proposal, an approved plan, a bounded real build, and evidence you can defend.

## Positioning

Unfinished Business is a **workshop around OpenCode**, not a replacement coding agent. OpenCode owns the model route, agent loop, native tools, tool permissions, execution, interruption, and native sessions. This product owns the four-stage workshop, exact-version approvals, dependency invalidation, evidence views, the first-run connection/discovery flow, and the Ghostlight interface.

The product is for a builder with an idea but no finished submission: a student at a hackathon, a solo maker on a short deadline, or a developer returning to a stalled project. It is not a multi-user platform, a hosted remote-code-execution service, or an autonomous deployer.

### Promise

- Make the next honest action obvious.
- Never turn a model reply into an approval.
- Never turn an unobserved result into evidence.
- Keep failures and empty states visible.
- Let a visitor understand the product before connecting an engine.

### Non-goals

- Remote access to a visitor's local repository.
- A public hosted sandbox with arbitrary execution.
- A second coding harness, inference client, or command executor.
- Silent paid-model fallback, fabricated usage metrics, testimonials, awards, or guaranteed outcomes.
- Automatic deployment, publication, or submission.

## Release truth (Phase 9)

The release candidate has one project story with three deployment modes:

| Mode | Browser can configure OpenCode? | OpenCode process | Persistence | Intended use |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `local` | Yes; password may be held in memory | Supplies it separately on loopback | `UB_DATA_DIR` | A developer on their own Linux machine |
| `private-hosted` | No; environment/secret store owns the URL and password | Loopback child process | Private persistent disk | Protected Render or self-hosted instance |
| `hosted-demo` | No | None | None for visitors | Public deterministic sample |

Maker edits only the isolated demo workspace under `UB_DATA_DIR`. The product does not mount an arbitrary local or hosted repository in this release. The Node check is a bounded child process, not an OS sandbox. App approvals constrain workflow transitions; they never override an OpenCode permission denial.

## The four roles

| Spirit | Stage | Function | Approval boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| Oracle | Clarify | Turn an unfinished idea into a product proposal and open questions | The user approves the product; the proposal alone is not approval |
| Architect | Plan | Draft one planning section against its dependencies | The user approves the exact current version and hash; revisions make old approval stale |
| Maker | Build | Perform a bounded native edit through OpenCode | A separate Maker scope is required; OpenCode still owns tool permission |
| Witness | Review | Inspect evidence in a fresh session and prepare review drafts | Notes are drafts, not a submitted article, video, or proof of success |

### Workshop interface promise

The workshop shows one primary task at a time. The project outline opens as a drawer, Activity & results appears only when there is an operation or check, and Project memory holds decisions, answers, assumptions, constraints, and unresolved questions. Model and permission controls are visible; native IDs, capability mappings, raw evidence, provider payloads, sessions, revert controls, export, and transcripts stay under Technical details or Advanced diagnostics. A correction to Project memory supersedes the prior entry and never changes an approval or draft.

## Three honest usage paths

| Path | What it is | What it is not |
|---|---|---|
| Hosted demo | A labeled deterministic walkthrough served without OpenCode, credentials, a session token, or visitor persistence | Not live inference; not a sandbox; not access to a visitor's repository |
| Private hosted | A password-protected workshop on a private disk with a loopback OpenCode child | Not a public sandbox; not access to a visitor's local checkout |
| Full local mode | The browser app, local API, and pinned OpenCode server on the builder's machine over loopback | Not a guarantee of free-model availability; not permission to widen tool scope |

The landing page must describe all three without implying that a hosted page can read a local checkout. The hosted demo's `/workshop` route explains that it is read-only and offers the guided example or local setup as exits.

## OpenCode-only claim

Approved language:

> OpenCode supplies the agent loop, model access, native tools, permissions, and sessions. Unfinished Business adds the four-stage workshop, exact-version approvals, dependency invalidation, an evidence ledger, and a first-run connection/discovery panel.

Models are discovered from the OpenCode catalog rather than assumed. New projects may use any model OpenCode reports as available, with an optional free/local-only policy and an optional spending limit. A paid or unknown-price remote route requires an explicit confirmation before its first request; the app never silently substitutes a model or treats a model reply as approval. The free `opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free` route remains one reported option when available, but availability is time-limited and account-dependent.

Provider API keys stay in OpenCode. The first-run panel accepts only the OpenCode server Basic-auth password, holds it in memory for local work, and never exposes a provider-key field.

## Landing information architecture

1. Hero: “Turn unfinished ideas into hackathon-ready builds.”
2. Value statement and OpenCode-only positioning.
3. Primary actions: try the example, watch the guided workflow, run live with OpenCode, set up locally.
4. Three ways to use it: hosted demo, private hosted, and full local.
5. Four-spirit workflow explanation.
6. Deterministic demo teaser with an explicit fixture label.
7. OpenCode controls and evidence preview.
8. Idea-to-tool recommendation preview.
9. Local setup command tabs sourced from tested documentation.
10. Privacy and security boundaries.
11. FAQ and final call to action.

## The guided demo's role

The deterministic example is the product's **onboarding proof** and the judge's **fast path to the value story**:

- **Onboarding:** a first-time visitor can complete the whole journey — unfinished idea → approved plan → bounded implementation → diff/tests → Witness evidence → next step — without an OpenCode account, provider key, model quota, or repository.
- **Judging:** the same interface contracts render live and fixture runs, so the demo demonstrates the approval, permission, progress, evidence, and recovery surfaces without pretending the fixture is a live session.
- **Trust:** the demo is explicit about what it cannot prove. The live native session remains `NOT_RUN`; reset affects only the fixture; the hosted demo cannot mutate anything.

The demo is a **guided example**, not a second product surface. It uses the production `RunInspector`, `SpiritCharacter`, `SpiritStageTabs`, `StatusChip`, and shared workflow schemas.

## Calls to action

| Action | Destination | Truthful expectation |
|---|---|---|
| Try the example | `/demo` | An interactive, scripted fixture; not live inference |
| Watch the guided workflow | `/demo?presentation=1` | A 90-second screen-recording path over the same fixture |
| Run live with OpenCode | `/workshop` | The real workflow; engine status is visible and may be unreachable |
| Connect OpenCode | Setup dialog | Instructions only; no connection is implied until the engine answers |
| Set up locally | `#local-setup` | Commands match `docs/LOCAL_SETUP.md` |
| Walk through the fixture | `/demo` | Representative states with fixture IDs |

## Prohibited claims

Do not add:

- testimonials, customer logos, star ratings, or “trusted by” statements;
- user counts, build counts, time-saved figures, or success rates without a measured source;
- awards, rankings, organizer endorsements, or partner claims not actually granted;
- “guaranteed working build,” “autonomous,” “fully hosted coding agent,” or “reads your repository”;
- live-inference language around the deterministic demo;
- claims that app approval overrides an OpenCode permission denial.

## Success criteria

A first-time visitor can explain:

1. what the product does;
2. who Oracle, Architect, Maker, and Witness are;
3. OpenCode's role and the no-second-harness boundary;
4. the difference between the deterministic demo, a hosted/private instance, and full local mode;
5. what the product cannot reach.

## 8. Demo fixture boundaries

The guided sample is a browser-bundled fixture, not a server response and not a parallel UI. The same fixture also feeds the landing preview, visual snapshots, and the sample evidence view; `src/web/content/landing.ts` holds copy and configuration only, with no second operation/evidence state.

```text
src/shared/workflow.ts   production Zod schemas + types
        │
        ├─ src/server/workflow/model.ts  hashing, migration, persistence helpers
        ├─ src/shared/demo.ts            versioned fixture + beats + landing preview
        ├─ src/web/demo/DemoPage.tsx     playback + shared components
        └─ src/web/landing/DemoTeaser.tsx landing preview from the same fixture
                    │
                    ├─ RunInspector
                    ├─ SpiritStageTabs (inspect variant)
                    ├─ SpiritCharacter / StatusChip / Brand
                    └─ pure playback reducer (no API calls)
```

`src/shared/demo.ts` has no `node:`, `fetch`, `process.env`, `Date.now`, or `Math.random`. Tests parse the fixture with the production schemas, recompute section hashes, and assert that the landing preview and guided sample report the same check and live-proof status. Every recorded result is labeled; the live session remains `NOT_RUN`.

In `hosted-demo` mode the server independently returns the fixture from `/api/project` and `/api/export`, returns a read-only connection status, rejects `/api/session` and every non-GET `/api/*` request, and never constructs an OpenCode connection.

## 9. Phase 9 release copy and boundary states

- Local mode copy says Maker edits the isolated demo workspace, not an arbitrary repository. The mode descriptor no longer claims workspace selection.
- Hosted-demo copy says there is no OpenCode, provider, session token, visitor persistence, or repository. `/workshop` is a read-only notice with exits to `/demo` and local setup.
- Private-hosted copy says the URL, password, and secrets are environment-managed; the browser cannot edit them.
- API copy distinguishes invalid session token, invalid origin, rate limit, concurrent mutation, request too large, stale revision, unknown native outcome, pending permission, and corrupt/busy state.
- Recommendation previews carry source and `verifiedAt` metadata. They describe only current capabilities and never imply an install, paid model, arbitrary shell, or approval.
- Evidence and Activity & results labels keep fixture results separate from live `NOT_RUN`/native results. No color or animation is the only status signal.
- The final accessibility matrix covers keyboard focus, dialog Escape, setup-tab arrow keys, 200% text zoom, 390px/wide layouts, overflow, reduced motion, contrast, and relevant screen-reader/live-region semantics.

| OpenCode compatibility | PASS — server 2.0.32, catalog, disposable session create/read/remove | No inference; no provider account; no agents/commands in the empty test config |
| Local fresh setup | PASS — health, mode, token, project, workshop route | OpenCode was not running during the local smoke |
| Hosted demo | PASS — fixture project, no token, `DEMO_READ_ONLY`, no engine, `/demo` HTML | Preview only; no public deployment |
